topic: What if you could copy and paste anything?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
COPY AND PASTE ANYTHING?

power.rule: anything you can see, as many times as you like
power.look: a selection box with marching ants and a COPY chip; a pop and a flash ring on PASTE

script.text: Copy a cookie. Paste. Free cookies, forever.
Copy your best friend. Paste. Okay, that's weird.
What if you could copy and paste anything?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: a copy can't come from nothing. One cookie, made from pure energy, needs every power plant on Earth running for over ten minutes. That's real.
So where are yours coming from?

science.claim: One cookie made from pure energy needs every power plant on Earth running for over ten minutes.
science.working: A 30 g cookie: E = mc^2 = 0.030 kg x (2.998e8 m/s)^2 = 2.70e15 J. The world's power plants generated 29,925 TWh of electricity in 2023 (about 31,000 TWh in 2025), an average output of 3.4 to 3.5e12 W. 2.70e15 J / 3.5e12 W = 760 s, about 12.7 minutes (13.2 at 2023's output). Over ten minutes holds for any cookie heavier than about 24 g. The on-screen schematic states the 30 g.
science.source: E = mc^2 (mass-energy equivalence); Ember, Global Electricity Review 2024 (world generation 2023: 29,925 TWh)

science.claim: A copy can't come from nothing.
science.working: Conservation of mass-energy: matter can't be created without the equivalent energy, so every pasted object needs its mass-energy from somewhere.

shots.note: Pip at the counter points at a cookie on a plate; a selection box draws round it
a second cookie pops in beside the first, with a flash ring
cookies paste themselves along the counter in rows; Pip cheers, the cat looks up
a finished worksheet (A+) next to a blank one; the box selects the finished sheet
a stack of finished sheets pops onto the desk; Pip leans back, smug
Mo waves on the landing by the lit doorway; the box selects Mo
a second Mo pops in; the two Mos turn and stare at each other
Pip, uneasy; both Mos soft behind him, staring at him
the premise over the city at dusk; Pip on the roof with a stack of cookies
Pip stops mid-bite and looks at the cookie
the pasted cookie in his mitten: its outline flickers, a ghost of the selection
1 cookie, 30 g, to E = mc2, to 2,700,000,000,000,000 joules counting up
every power plant on Earth lights up; a dial runs past ten minutes to 12:42
Pip, worried; the light starts to turn red
the city's lights go out in a sweep toward him, the string lights die; the sky goes red
